info.title: QUANTEX Developer API
info.description: QUANTEX Developer API: Brokers & pairs, Payouts, Economic news, Account & usage, Signal checker, Candles (OHLC), Historical candles, Live ticks, Live signals & results, Future signals, Signal stream (SSE). Every answer uses the envelope {"ok", "data" | "error", "meta"}. Binary options trading carries high risk; data is analysis, not a guarantee.

get.summary: Status of the API, data feeds, Telegram bot and payments, and open incidents (the same as quantexbot.pro/status). status: operational, degraded, partial_outage, major_outage or maintenance; each component: operational, degraded, down or unknown. No key needed.
Your plan, its limits, what you used and the key in use.
Requests per day and per endpoint.
Supported brokers and whether their data feed is live.
Pairs of a broker: OTC or Live, category, open now, current payout.

get.summary: OHLC candles (UTC), oldest first. M1 gives every stored minute (only closed minutes are stored). M5 and higher give only closed candles: the running candle is left out until its period has ended (at 12:23 the newest M5 candle is the one of 12:15; 12:20 arrives complete after 12:25). Without date: the most recent candles; with date: that UTC day (within your plan's history). Brokers give no real volume, so volume is an activity score: the candle's range (60 %) and body (40 %) against the average of the 20 candles before it, x100 (100 = normal, 0 when fewer than 20 earlier candles). payout = the broker's payout % when the candle opened.

parameters.name: broker
parameters.description: Broker: quotex, tradowix or binolla (the ones your plan covers: Candle Basic 1, Candle Data 2, Full Market Data all 3; otherwise error broker_not_in_plan).

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Number of candles (newest last). Without date: 1-2000 (Market Data plans; 1-1000 on other plans), default 100. With date: 1-1440, default the whole day (M1: 1440 candles).

get.summary: Historical OHLC candles (UTC) of a range of days, oldest first, straight from the QUANTEX servers: every closed candle of every day, the same data the QUANTEX checker uses. M1: up to 7 days per request (10 080 candles); M5 and higher: up to 31 days. Same fields as /v1/candles. How far back you may ask depends on your plan (error history_limit).

parameters.name: broker
parameters.description: Broker: quotex, tradowix or binolla (the ones your plan covers: Candle Basic 1, Candle Data 2, Full Market Data all 3; otherwise error broker_not_in_plan).

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: Last UTC day, YYYY-MM-DD (default: the same as from).

get.summary: The newest live tick of up to 20 pairs (QUOTEX, TRADOWIX and BINOLLA): price, bid, ask and the exact time in milliseconds (UTC), plus the broker's running M1 candle (open, high, low, close = price, seconds_left). Put it on top of /v1/candles and your chart moves exactly like the broker's. fresh=false: no new tick for 2 minutes (market closed or paused). available=false: no tick for this pair right now. For a moving chart use the tick stream (/v1/stream/ticks) instead of asking again and again.

parameters.name: pairs
parameters.description: Up to 20 pair symbols, comma-separated, e.g. EURUSD_otc,BTCUSD_otc.

get.summary: Server-Sent Events: a "tick" event (same object as in /v1/ticks) every time the price of one of your pairs changes, checked about 4 times a second. When a minute closes the next tick carries the new candle, so a chart fed by this stream draws every candle like the broker. The stream closes after 5 minutes with event "reconnect"; open it again (EventSource does this by itself). At most 2 open streams per account.

schema.description: Server-Sent Events: event = tick, data = one tick as JSON (see /v1/ticks).

post.summary: Check a signal list: WIN / LOSS / NO_DATA for each signal, with martingale (MTG) steps.

signals.description: Up to 200 objects: {"pair":"EURUSD_otc","time":"14:05","direction":"BUY","timeframe":"M1"}. Direction BUY/CALL or PUT/SELL.

text.description: Or paste a list in the bot format, one per line: "M1 EURUSD-OTC 14:05 CALL".

timezone.description: UTC offset of the signal times in hours, e.g. 6 or -3 (default 6).

get.summary: Upcoming economic events with the expected direction (bias) and the pairs to trade. The direction combines forecast vs previous, how the market reacted to past releases of the same event, the trend and AI; unclear news is skipped, and a currency / pair never gets two directions at the same minute. days=1 is the rest of today (in your timezone), 2 adds tomorrow, 3 the day after.

Live signals the QUANTEX bot delivered, and their results. active = signals waiting for entry or running. events = signal.created and signal.result, oldest first; ask again with since=next_cursor (every 2-5 s) to get only new events. Without since: the latest events. A signal has its entry and expiry time (UTC), so your own bot can post it at once; its result arrives later with the same id. result: WIN (mtg_level 0 = direct, 1 = after one martingale step), LOSS (also after one martingale step) or NO_DATA.

parameters.name: since
parameters.description: Cursor from next_cursor of the last answer.

parameters.name: broker
parameters.description: Broker(s), comma-separated: quotex, tradowix, binolla. Empty = all.

get.summary: One signal by id, with its result when it is known (status pending, running or settled).
Settled signals of one UTC day with a summary: wins, mtg_wins (won after one martingale step), losses, win_rate (with one martingale step) and win_rate_no_mtg. Up to 30 days back.

parameters.name: broker
parameters.description: Broker(s), comma-separated: quotex, tradowix, binolla. Empty = all.

parameters.name: tf
parameters.description: Timeframe(s), comma-separated, e.g. M1,M5. Empty = all.

parameters.name: pair
parameters.description: Pair(s), comma-separated, e.g. EURUSD_otc. Empty = all.

post.summary: Make a future signal list with the QUANTEX future engine (the same as the bot's Future Signal): every minute of the window is back-tested on the last five days of each market. Answers 202 with a job at once; the list is usually ready in a few seconds (longer for many markets): GET /v1/jobs/{id}. Times are in the timezone you send; only times from now + 2 minutes are listed.

mode.description: otc (default), live, blackout or whiteout (blackout / whiteout give times without a direction).

timezone.description: UTC offset in hours, e.g. 6 or -3 (default 6).

filter.description: Martingale filter: non (default), mtg1 or mtg2 - a slot also counts as won when it wins within 1 / 2 martingale steps.

direction.description: call, put or both (default). Ignored for blackout / whiteout.

level.description: high (default, fewer and stronger signals) or medium (more signals).

pairs.description: Pairs to use, e.g. ["EURUSD_otc","USDJPY_otc"]. Empty = every open pair.

get.summary: State of a future list job: queued, running, done (result.signals) or failed (error). Jobs are kept 7 days.

Server-Sent Events: every new signal.created / signal.result the moment it arrives (id = cursor). The stream closes after 5 minutes with event "reconnect"; reconnect with the Last-Event-ID header (EventSource does this by itself) so nothing is missed. At most 2 open streams per account.

schema.description: Server-Sent Events: id = cursor, event = signal.created | signal.result, data = the event as JSON.

parameters.name: since
parameters.description: Start after this cursor (default: only new events).
